trigger: archival on Amazon S3 Glacier to "enforce regulatory and compliance controls"
answer: S3 Glacier vault with a Vault Lock policy (WORM controls, locked from future edits)
trap: The S3 lifecycle policy option only transitions or expires objects and cannot enforce compliance; the S3 ACL options manage access but cannot enforce compliance controls.

trigger: "all changes to the items stored in the DynamoDB tables must be logged in near real-time"
answer: DynamoDB Streams → Lambda → Kinesis Data Streams → Kinesis Data Analytics → SNS
trap: CloudTrail records control-plane API calls, not item-level changes; the Lambda-direct-to-KDA option fails because KDA only accepts KDS or Firehose as sources.
memory_hook: item changes = Streams; KDA needs KDS

trigger: "many files are processed twice" with more instances added to an Auto Scaling group reading a shared EFS directory
answer: S3 upload → S3 trigger → Lambda enqueues to SQS; workers read the queue, Auto Scaling on queue depth
trap: The Lambda-plus-EventBridge-to-SQS option is a roundabout way to propagate the upload event; the hourly EFS-to-S3 cron job loses files when the Lambda fails with no queue to retry.
memory_hook: Upload event → queue → workers, not cron

trigger: "both stateful and stateless client-server communications" via API Gateway APIs
answer: Amazon API Gateway REST APIs for stateless client-server communication and WebSocket APIs for stateful, full-duplex communication (option C)
trap: Option D makes REST stateful, but REST APIs are HTTP-based and stateless; option B reverses the pairing by making WebSocket stateless, which ignores its persistent full-duplex connection.

trigger: 429 Too Many Requests from multiple API methods while Lambda functions are never invoked, plus a separate quota for premium customers
answer: API Gateway account-level calls-per-second limit; usage plans with API keys as client identifiers for per-client premium throttling
trap: The per-method limit option fails because errors across several methods mean the account-level limit was hit; Lambda-level throttling targets in usage plans cannot be defined.
memory_hook: Lambda not invoked = API Gateway throttled; API keys + usage plans

trigger: "only the most frequently accessed results are available as cached data locally while backing up all results on Amazon S3"
answer: AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway in Cached Volume mode: hot data cached on-premises, full volume in S3
trap: The Stored Volume option keeps the entire data set on-premises, which fails the requirement that only frequently accessed results stay local.
memory_hook: Cached = hot local, full copy in S3

trigger: "140 TB" archive due in S3 by Monday over a "10-Gbps Direct Connect connection" with a private VIF in place
answer: Public virtual interface on the existing Direct Connect connection, then copy to S3 over it
trap: Option B's private VIF reaches only VPC private IPs, not S3. Option C (Snowball Edge) takes about a week end to end, missing the deadline.
memory_hook: S3 is public = public VIF; Snowball is for weeks, DX is for days

trigger: "without moving away from the underlying relational database schema" plus "work on a global scale" across regions
answer: Amazon Aurora Global Database: one relational database spanning regions with fast local reads
trap: DynamoDB Global Tables give multi-region read and write, but it is NoSQL and abandons the relational schema the company must keep.

trigger: Redshift cluster must operate or be restored within five hours in case of disaster, most cost-effective
answer: Automated Redshift snapshots copied cross-Region, restored in the other Region, with the cluster defined by a CloudFormation StackSet
trap: Two always-on clusters in two Regions (Kinesis or UNLOAD/LOAD cron jobs) double cost; the Auto Scaling groups across AZs option fails because Redshift cannot use Auto Scaling groups.
memory_hook: Cheap DR = copied snapshots, not a second live cluster

trigger: S3TA "did not result in an accelerated transfer" with uploads from the internet
answer: No transfer charges: S3 bills no data-in fees, and S3 Transfer Acceleration bills only for accelerated transfers
trap: The S3 plus S3TA option fails because neither applies: inbound internet data to S3 is free and unaccelerated S3TA transfers are not billed
memory_hook: Data in is free; unaccelerated S3TA is free

trigger: "shared and centrally-managed VPCs" for business units needing high interconnectivity within one organization
answer: VPC sharing via Resource Access Manager: share one or more subnets with accounts in the same AWS Organization
trap: The VPC peering option sounds like connectivity, but peering does not centralise management, and an owner cannot share the whole VPC, so the Share-the-VPC option fails.
memory_hook: Centrally managed VPC = share subnets via RAM

trigger: "huge delays in uploading large video files" to S3 from overseas research facilities
answer: S3 Transfer Acceleration plus S3 multipart uploads: edge-network ingest and parallel parts together speed large uploads
trap: Multiple Direct Connect links take months to provision and are overkill; the Site-to-Site VPN option stays on the public internet and adds no speed for S3 uploads.
memory_hook: Distant uploads = Transfer Acceleration; big files = multipart

trigger: 200 TB to S3 "in the shortest possible time" over Direct Connect or VPN bandwidth
answer: AWS Snowball Edge devices, three units (80 TB each), shipped to AWS for import into S3
trap: The Direct Connect and VPN options look fast, but at 500 Mbps and 1 Gbps, 200 TB takes roughly 40 and 20 days, far longer than the 5-7 day Snowball turnaround.
memory_hook: Over 20 TB of bandwidth-bound data: ship it

trigger: "I/O intensive" workload "constrained on the IOPS" needing +3,000 IOPS per instance, "MOST cost-efficient"
answer: Resize the EBS gp2 volume from 3 TB to 4 TB: gp2 baseline is 3 IOPS per GiB, so +1,000 GiB adds 3,000 IOPS
trap: Option C, io1 at 12,000 IOPS, works but costs more per GB-month; option B (EFS) costs about 3x gp2 per GB, and option A (S3) cannot serve frequent random updates
memory_hook: gp2 = 3 IOPS per GiB, so add GiB to add IOPS

trigger: "disaster recovery strategy for all the Amazon RDS databases" with options on snapshot sharing, RTO, and Read Replica failover
answer: Manual DB snapshots copied and shared across Regions and accounts; RTO as hours to restore; Read Replicas and backups cross-Region
trap: Read Replica failover is manual, unlike Multi-AZ; automated snapshots cannot be shared, only manual snapshots (up to 20 accounts); RPO, not RTO, measures data loss.
memory_hook: RTO = hours back up; RPO = data lost
